# `Q-2-57` — Attribute List After Code Block Language

> A fenced code block's opening line has a language word followed by a `{...}` attribute list.

## What this means

The opening line of a fenced code block takes either one language word
(```` ```python ````) or one attribute list in braces (```` ```{#id .python} ````),
not both. This error fires when a language word is followed by an attribute
list, as in ```` ```python {.marimo} ````.

The parser reports the error at the point where the word ends and adds a hint
that rewrites your own attribute list with the language moved inside the
braces, using the identifier, classes and values you actually wrote. The hint
shows two forms:

- `{#id .python .cls key=val}` — a plain code block with the language as its
  first class.
- `{python #id .cls key=val}` — an executable cell for the `python` engine.

Which one you want depends on whether the code should run. Pandoc reads
`python {.cls}` as a code block, so the first form keeps that meaning.

## How to fix

Move the language word inside the braces:

````markdown
```{#id .python .marimo}      <!-- code block, correct -->
```{python .marimo}           <!-- executable cell, correct -->
```python {.marimo}           <!-- triggers Q-2-57 -->
````

A word followed by something other than a braced list (for example
```` ```python .marimo ````) does not get this hint.

`qmd-syntax-helper` does not rewrite this form, because it cannot know whether
a code block or an executable cell was intended.

## Example

The parser flags this input:

````markdown
```python {.marimo}
code
```
````
